attempts.label: CRCNS:fcx-2
attempts.entry_title: Frontotemporal theta systems in working memory (Johnson et al. 2018)
attempts.summary: In this intracranial dataset the paper's behavioural results and the theta peak in medial temporal and frontal phase locking held up, while sustained theta power and the shift of theta directionality after the test cue did not. The directionality result rests on placing windows where the trial table puts the task events; in the deposited code's windows, 1.5 s later, it holds in part. The phase-amplitude coupling findings could not be tested, as the Methods' phase-slope index selects almost no phase-directing units and the code's version selects as many from shuffled data. Equal response times across conditions hold only with the dataset's summary file, not its trial tables. Electrode and trial counts matched.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Johnson, Adams, Solbakk, Endestad, Larsson, Ivanovic, Meling, Lin and Knight (2018) on CRCNS data set fcx-2, which holds the preprocessed intracranial EEG of the 10 subjects (254 bipolar MTL, PFC and OFC electrodes) in the visuospatial working memory task, their trial tables and the paper's analysis scripts. It checks behaviour, electrode and trial counts, ERPs, task-induced power, PLV, theta PSI, cross-spectral PSI and theta PAC by condition.

outcomes.notes: Judged on reading (c) of the amended criterion, condition as one numeric term (identity 1, spatial 2, temporal 3) on 30 subject-condition values, F the squared t of the slope with p from F(1,28). Accuracy (empirical logit) gives F(1,28) = 0.16, p = 0.70 over all trials and 0.44, p = 0.51 over kept trials; the paper gives F < 0.10, p > 0.75, so the effect is absent here too but the F is above the paper's bound. Response time from docs/summary_file.csv, whose condition means and SDs are the paper's (1659 +- 701, 1335 +- 574, 1475 +- 734 ms), gives F(1,28) = 2.41, p = 0.13, against the paper's F < 2.55, p > 0.12. The outcome rests on two assumptions: the numeric coding, which the criterion states, and judging response time on summary_file.csv. With the trial tables' response times (condition means 1744, 1237, 1292 ms, also within the paper's SDs) reading (c) finds an effect (F(1,28) = 12.33, p = 0.0015 over all trials; 11.48, p = 0.0021 over kept trials), and the outcome would be not reproduced. The revision searched for the source of the file's response times among summaries of the trial tables (means and medians over correct, all or kept trials, other subjects' rows, blocks of 40 trials, trial type): 9 of 30 values are matched, all by the mean over correct trials of s6, s8 and s9, and none of the other 7 subjects' values. Reported, not judged: under (a) and (b) response time differs by condition in both sources (summary_file.csv spatial against identity p = 0.0018, 3-level p = 0.0076; trial tables p < 0.001), and accuracy over all trials differs between spatial and identity (p = 0.023) but not under the 3-level term (p = 0.054; 0.37 over kept trials). What the answer changed. The first run judged the claim on readings (a) and (b), found a response-time effect under both and recorded not reproduced, and asked whether the numeric reading should be named (questions/crcns-fcx-2.yaml). The reader amended the criterion to judge on (c), on the printed F(1,28), and kept (a) and (b) as reported. Under (c) the outcome is reproduced, with assumed set because it depends on the response-time source.
deviations: Accuracy enters the logit model as the empirical logit of each subject and condition, log((k + 0.5) / (n - k + 0.5)), in a linear mixed model on 30 rows, as some subjects are at 100% in a condition; the paper does not specify its logit model further.

The response times of the trial tables differ from those of summary_file.csv in 7 of 10 subjects, and no summary of the trial tables tried gives the file's values for those 7. Both were tested. The outcome is judged on summary_file.csv, as an assumption: its condition means and SDs are the ones the paper prints (Results, paragraph 2), so it holds the values the paper's models were fitted to, while the trial tables' means are not the paper's.

The F of reading (c) is the squared t of the condition slope in a REML linear mixed model with a subject random intercept (statsmodels), with p from F(1,28), the residual degrees of freedom the criterion names; MATLAB's fitlme, which the criterion cites, was not run.

statistics.n: 254 electrodes in 10 subjects

outcomes.notes: With the code's subject-wide cluster null (all of a subject's electrodes in one test, as erp_compute.m runs it) and the code's baseline, 1 of 254 electrodes has a significant cluster in the trial table's windows (s9 FORA_11, encoding t test, p = 0.036), and the criterion allows none; in the code's windows 1 does too (s5 OFG14). Subtracting each trial's own baseline mean leaves 0 electrodes significant under the subject-wide null, which would be reproduced, so the outcome rests on the baseline as the code subtracts it. With a per-electrode null 27, 22 and 13 electrodes are significant (code's baseline, per-trial baseline, code's windows), against 25.4 expected by chance over two tests. The effect is small and isolated, but the criterion is no electrode.
deviations: Assumed, the windows placed by the trial table and the descriptor (encoding [-1.5, 0] s and the precue delay [-0.9, 0] s of encmain, postcue [-1.2, -0.3] s of proc, baseline [-0.85, -0.65] s of pre), 1.5 s earlier than the deposited code's latencies ([0, 1.5], [0.6, 1.5], [0.3, 1.2], [0.65, 0.85]). The first sample of each derived segment is the table's epoch start, and the 900 and 1150 ms delay trials part where the table puts the first delay-dependent event in each segment (proc ERPs from -0.25 to 0.75 s, p down to 0.005 against 200 permutations, around the response screen at -0.3 s) and not where the code's windows put it (proc 1.0 to 2.0 s, p 0.29 to 0.94). The code's windows are run as a variant for ERPs, power, PLV and both PSI measures. If the deposited scripts produced the paper's figures, the paper's numbers come from the code's windows, so the main reading tests the claims against the events the Methods describe and does not recompute the paper's numbers. The table's windows start 0 (encoding), 0.3 (postcue) and 0.65 s (baseline) after a segment's first sample; joining each trial's segments shows this leaves baseline power unchanged and lowers theta power only in the first 250 ms of encoding.

The baseline subtracted is the mean over trials of each trial's baseline mean, as erp_compute.m does (lines 84 to 88, nanmean(pretrial.trial)); the claims file's "subtracting the temporal mean of the baseline" is also read per trial, as a variant.
FieldTrip's filters and cluster test are reimplemented in Python (fir1 design, two-pass, zero padding to 7.5 s; cluster sums, 1000 permutations, p doubled for the two-tailed t test).

outcomes.statement: Theta-band PSI showed frontal-to-MTL leads during the precue delay and shifted toward MTL leads (a bidirectional network) after the test cue, for MTL to PFC and MTL to OFC pairs.
outcomes.source: Results, Theta oscillations direct local and long-range activity, paragraph 2 (The 900-ms pre- and postcue delay data segments); Figure 3B
outcomes.quote: The precue delay was characterized by unidirectional frontal-to-MTL theta band connectivity (threshold z < −1.96, p < 0.05) ... directionality shifted between frontotemporal regions from a unidirectional to bidirectional network (postcue > precue, MTL–PFC: F 1,342 > 139, p < 4 × 10 −27 ; MTL–OFC: F 1,604 > 268, p < 4 × 10 −50 ; Fig 3B )

statistics.n: 9 subjects, 172 electrode pairs
7 subjects, 303 electrode pairs

outcomes.notes: Judged with the PSI of the Methods (Nolte, trial-averaged cross-spectrum, frequencies of one signal shuffled for the null) from sliding 3-cycle windows, as M5 gives it, in the trial table's windows. Neither part holds in either network: precue mean z is 0.25 (MTL-PFC) and 0.01 (MTL-OFC), with 45 against 55 and 82 against 87 pairs below -1.96 and above 1.96, and postcue does not exceed precue (MTL-PFC raw p = 0.27; MTL-OFC raw PSI falls, p < 0.0001). Other readings. The code's single window is a variant the criterion does not judge, as M5 fixes sliding windows; it gives part (2) for MTL-PFC on raw PSI only (p = 0.014) with MTL-OFC raw PSI falling (p = 0.001). In the code's windows sliding windows give part (1) in both networks and part (2) for MTL-OFC on raw PSI only (p = 0.027), also partial, and the single window gives part (2) in neither. The code's own form of PSI gives both parts in both networks in the code's windows and part (1) and part (2) in one network each in the table's, but with trials shuffled it passes 57% of pairs (z SD 44), as many as on the real data, so it is not used. The sliding-window z is also too wide (SD 2.3 with trials shuffled), which bears on part (1) only; the single window is near nominal (SD 0.92, 2.2% above 1.96). The outcome rests on the window placement: in the code's windows the claims file's sliding reading would be partial. The placement follows the events as the data place them (delay-jitter test), but if the deposited scripts produced the paper's figures, the paper's PSI comes from the code's windows, so the table's placement tests the claim against the events the Methods describe and does not recompute what the paper did. The pair counts are 170 and 289 (expected 172 and 303).
deviations: The sliding 3-cycle windows of M5 cannot be placed inside a 900 ms segment at 3 Hz (a 1 s window); here they run into the zero padding of the 4 s segment. The code's single Hanning window over the segment (psi_compute.m, FieldTrip mtmfft, which ignores t_ftimwin) is a variant, and so is the code's own form of PSI (psianalysis.m, conjugate added), which averages per-trial PSI and z-scores it against a null built from trial-averaged coherency.
The mixed model with random intercepts for subject and pair is computed as the within-pair F test of interval (equal for two intervals per pair), with all pairs after the 7 exclusions.

PSI is one value per pair over 3 to 7 Hz, and the null pairs one signal's coherency at each frequency with the other's at a shuffled frequency. The Methods' "electrode pair and frequency-resolved" PSI with a 2 Hz bandwidth, and a null that shuffles the order of the coherency spectrum, were not run.

Assumed, the windows placed by the trial table and the descriptor (encoding [-1.5, 0] s and the precue delay [-0.9, 0] s of encmain, postcue [-1.2, -0.3] s of proc, baseline [-0.85, -0.65] s of pre), 1.5 s earlier than the deposited code's latencies ([0, 1.5], [0.6, 1.5], [0.3, 1.2], [0.65, 0.85]). The first sample of each derived segment is the table's epoch start, and the 900 and 1150 ms delay trials part where the table puts the first delay-dependent event in each segment (proc ERPs from -0.25 to 0.75 s, p down to 0.005 against 200 permutations, around the response screen at -0.3 s) and not where the code's windows put it (proc 1.0 to 2.0 s, p 0.29 to 0.94). The code's windows are run as a variant for ERPs, power, PLV and both PSI measures. If the deposited scripts produced the paper's figures, the paper's numbers come from the code's windows, so the main reading tests the claims against the events the Methods describe and does not recompute the paper's numbers. The table's windows start 0 (encoding), 0.3 (postcue) and 0.65 s (baseline) after a segment's first sample; joining each trial's segments shows this leaves baseline power unchanged and lowers theta power only in the first 250 ms of encoding.

findings.statement: The derived data's time axes put each segment's first sample at -1.5 s, and that sample is the trial table's epoch start (encmain at column H, first stimulus onset; proc 0.3 s before column I, test cue offset; pre about 0.1 s after column G), so the task events lie 1.5 s earlier on the time axes than 0 s suggests. The deposited scripts cut their windows from the time axes as if 0 s were stimulus onset, test cue offset minus 0.3 s and start screen minus 0.9 s. The data side with the table: the 900 and 1150 ms delay trials part where the table puts the first delay-dependent event of each segment (proc ERPs from -0.25 to 0.75 s, p down to 0.005 against 200 permutations) and not where the scripts' windows put it (proc 1.0 to 2.0 s, p 0.29 to 0.94).

The response times of docs/summary_file.csv, which the descriptor says are "calculated on all correct trials", differ from the mean over correct trials of the per-trial tables in 7 of 10 subjects (s1 identity 1948 against 2348 ms), and no other summary of the trial tables tried (medians, all or kept trials, other subjects' rows, blocks of 40 trials, trial type) gives them. The paper's condition means are those of summary_file.csv. Its accuracies do equal the per-trial tables.

For s10 the trial table's epoch columns are not on the derived data's sample grid (offsets of 97.1 to 98.1 samples from column G, about 114 for two trials, and fractional offsets for H and I), and its trialinfo does not equal the trial table's columns.
The descriptor gives fsample 1000 for the derived structures; s8 and s9 are at 512 Hz (as its note on the trial table says).

The deposited psianalysis.m multiplies the Fourier coefficients without conjugating one of them, so its "cross-spectral density" and phase slope are not the PSI of Nolte et al. that the Methods cite. It also z-scores the trial mean of per-trial PSI against a null built from trial-averaged coherency, a different statistic; with the conjugate added, this form passes z > 1.96 for 57% of electrodes and pairs when one signal's trials are shuffled against the other's, as many as on the real data (56%), and its selection rates are of the order of the paper's counts of phase-directing units (31% to 49%). The Methods' PSI passes 0% to 0.1% with trials shuffled.

subtracterp.m with ncond = 3 selects the temporal trials by trialinfo column 5 == 2 (the delay length column, 900 or 1150), so the temporal condition is empty; pacanalysis.m sizes its amplitude matrix with an undefined variable `freq`; and dirpac_compute.m calls pacanalysis with six arguments while it takes four, so the deposited PAC scripts cannot run as given.

The Methods describe PSI from sliding 3-cycle windows (dt = 3/f) at 3 to 7 Hz on 900 ms segments; a 3-cycle window at 3 Hz is 1 s long and cannot be placed in the segment. The deposited code uses one Hanning window over the segment.

The behavioural models are said to have "3 condition-fixed effects" but are reported as F(1,28); with one value per subject and condition, F(1,28) is what condition as a single numeric term gives, and on summary_file.csv that reading gives the paper's p > 0.12 for response time.

Question for the authors. Were the behavioural mixed models fitted with condition as one numeric term (and if so, with which coding), on the per-subject values of docs/summary_file.csv, and how were those response times computed? The printed F(1,28) fits a numeric term on 30 subject-condition values. On summary_file.csv that model finds no response-time effect (p = 0.13); on the trial tables' response times it finds one (p = 0.0015), so the outcome of behavior-no-difficulty-difference rests on these choices.

Question for the authors. Which form of PSI produced the reported PSI z values and the counts of phase-directing electrodes (the Methods' Nolte PSI on the trial-averaged cross-spectrum, or the code's mean of per-trial PSI against trial-averaged coherency), with which spectral window, and were the analysis windows cut 1.5 s later on the derived time axes than the trial table places the events, as the deposited scripts do? The Methods' PSI selects at most 3 phase-directing units per system here, and the code's form selects as many with trials shuffled as on the real data, so crossspectral-equal-strength and the PAC claims are blocked.

disagreements.reason: Accuracy shows no effect under either reading (numeric term F 0.16, p 0.70; F 0.44, p 0.51). Response time shows no effect only with the summary_file.csv values (F 2.41, p 0.13). With the per-trial tables it does differ (F 12.3, p 0.0015 all trials; F 11.5, p 0.002 kept trials), and the two sources disagree in 7 of 10 subjects. The summary_file.csv values are of unknown provenance and were chosen because they match the paper (B2).

Cell 32. Single-window (Methods) PSI, the post-versus-pre test fails in both networks (p 0.27, 0.56). Sliding-window PSI on raw values, OFC passes (p 0.027), PFC fails (p 0.079), which is the criterion's partial case. The code's PSI form passes both networks on raw PSI (p < 1e-4), but its z part rests on a miscalibrated null (B3).

entries.name: johnson-2018
entries.title: Frontotemporal theta systems in working memory (Johnson et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Johnson, Adams, Solbakk, Endestad, Larsson, Ivanovic, Meling, Lin and Knight (2018) on CRCNS data set fcx-2, which holds the preprocessed intracranial EEG of the 10 subjects (254 bipolar MTL, PFC and OFC electrodes) in the visuospatial working memory task, their trial tables and the paper's analysis scripts. It checks behaviour, electrode and trial counts, ERPs, task-induced power, PLV, theta PSI, cross-spectral PSI and theta PAC by condition.
